direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is incredibly bland and boring, as it tries to be a lighthearted movie but doesn't know what it wants to be, playing it both too safe and too hard as it tries to be a family movie while going after young adults, all while leaning on the Taika comedy and flavor that was funny seven years ago but isn't anymore (Jojo Rabbit is the best it's ever going to be), and it throws so many colors at you that it's like watching a kaleidoscope, with the whole movie feeling like it was shot during golden hour because of its interest in the sun; the direction on a microscale is unbearable and such a slog to get through, as all the performances, dialogue, scenes, and relationships are boring; the storytelling is almost nonexistent, as there is barely any plot and the movie is a slog to get through even the most basic story; the tension is nonexistent, as I don't relate to or care about any of these characters, so when bad things happen to them, you don't care, and the movie is too feel-good for characters I don't care about

performance.comments: Just not a good actress, and this role doesn't play to the strengths of the monotonous, emo character she always plays, since a joyful robot is the antithesis of that; she has no charm or charisma here, making it very boring, and she keeps picking the worst movies that highlight how she's not a good actress, as she typecast herself into one type of role that she can't step away from, and she's not good in that type of role either, making her washed in her mid-twenties; I think the Jenna Ortega experiment is done, and I'm not interested in a Jenna Ortega project anymore; Inde Navarrette has officially snatched her chain

At a certain point, everyone says 'Amy Adams, fire your agent,' but I think she's just the issue now, as she keeps picking these bad movies, and she's not good in this one either, giving a very forced performance that doesn't feel natural with no chemistry with Jenna Ortega; this is just Amy Adams's new normal now, since not everybody gets a run that lasts forever, and hers is done
Just plays Natasha Lyonne, as I've seen her play this character so many times, and there's nothing special about it

cast.comments: Everyone just tries to do the Taika Waititi shtick, and it's not good, as the shtick is done

story.comments: The concept is dumb, as I don't know what the messaging is supposed to be, since it seems to want us to be more human and cherish human connection while using an AI as the conduit, delivering an anti-robot message through a robot and critiquing how we artificially create companionship without ever finding answers before the ending just happens; the plot structure is super linear, with an ending that's a bad fast-forward where you don't understand what happened to the characters, and the climax is so poorly written that I really don't understand its purpose or why it happened; character writing is terrible, as I did not care about a single one of these characters, since I'm not going to empathize with an AI that, for how humane it's trying to be, is still a robot at the end of the day, and I didn't care about the teenage character or Amy Adams's character at all, which is a problem for a feel-good movie that requires you to care about its characters, making it such a forgettable movie

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is so boring and bland, trying so hard to use the Taika Waititi shtick that doesn't work anymore, as he's gotten stale and lost his touch; the humor tries so hard to go for that silly Taika Waititi humor, but it's not funny anymore, and I laughed maybe one time in this whole movie; the symbolism is a bad message about being more human, caring about human interaction, and being more present in the world, told through a robot, which makes me reject anything it tries to tell me, and Robot Dreams is like Citizen Kane compared to this, since it delivered the same message without even using dialogue, showing how easy this message is to tell without overcomplicating it like this movie does; the foreshadowing is there, but the ending makes no sense, as the movie is super slow and then speedruns the ending, so you don't understand why anything is happening

score.comments: Well composed and somewhat makes the movie feel more light-hearted

cinematography.comments: Genuinely so boring and bland, with a lot of boring shots, and while it tries to be a kaleidoscope at moments, it just ends up tacky and nauseating; the playful handheld shots looking up and out the window as the solar flare comes in are actually well shot, but there are so many solar flares that it feels like, we get it, the movie's about the sun

editing.comments: A lot of boring editing with a lot of sharp cuts, making it feel tacky, boring, and lazy

sound.comments: Honestly not that good, and not that great for a movie about robots

production_design.comments: Looks like a fake future and a fake movie, very cheaply put together like a B-movie, so whoever designed this movie didn't do a good job

makeup.comments: Fine but cheap, mostly just some blood

costumes.comments: Okay, doing a little bit of a futuristic take on clothing, but it's not that amazing

review.pacing: Unbearably slow, to the point where the people I was with said this might be the longest two-hour movie they've ever seen, and I couldn't agree more, and then for no reason the ending is super fast, like a fast-forward to make up for the slow pacing, causing you to miss what's going on; you could cut a good amount out, but honestly, they just shouldn't have made the movie
review.climax: A big fast-forward where I don't know what's going on or why things are happening, as stuff just happens, making it a dumb ending
review.tone: Tries to be a feel-good movie but doesn't know what demographic it's catering to, trying to cater to everybody and, by doing that, catering to no one, and while it tries to go for YA, it doesn't do a good job of that; it very much feels like a Taika Waititi movie, but in 2026, that shtick is washed
review.final_notes: Saw an early screening; it's clear Sony has given up on this movie since there's been no marketing for it, and with critics already panning it, I know for a fact it's going to bomb
review.overall: Overall, 'Klara and the Sun' is genuinely a washed movie, with Taika Waititi washed, Jenna Ortega beyond washed, and Amy Adams in her new normal of bad movies, and on top of that, it's a snooze fest so boring that I kept checking my watch only to see two minutes had passed, making it the longest two-hour movie I've been to; Taika's shtick isn't funny anymore, and this movie should put him in director's jail
